mutants.expected_detection: structural_match_accuracy and word_recovery_rate drop below 128/128: for corrected codewords with data content varying at position 3 (1-indexed, corrected_codeword[2]), data[0] now incorrectly reflects the parity bit at position 1 (corrected_codeword[0]) instead, causing data[3:0] mismatches against the reference on many of the 128 exhaustive codewords, including error-free codewords where the confused parity/data bits differ.

Exhaustive simulation of all 128 codewords will show corrected_codeword mismatches for the 112 single-bit-error cases where the syndrome ordering diverges from the reference (s1 and s2 swapped in the syndrome vector), causing the wrong bit to be flipped during correction; structural_match_accuracy and functional_equivalence will drop below 128/128 and FAIL.

Exhaustive 128-codeword simulation comparing corrected_codeword and error_detected against the reference will show mismatches: codewords with syndrome==3'd4 (position 4, a parity bit) will incorrectly flip codeword[4] (position 5) instead of codeword[3] (position 4), causing wrong corrected_codeword and downstream wrong data bits for all codewords that map to syndrome value 4, breaking exact match on all 128 vectors required by FR1.

For all 16 error-free codewords, error_detected should be 0 in both reference and submission (both would already agree there), but this mutant stuck-at-zero forces error_detected to always be 0 even for the 112 single-bit-error codewords where the reference asserts error_detected=1, causing mismatches on FR3-relevant vectors; critically for FR2 the corrected_codeword logic is also broken because the syndrome comparisons are shifted, causing corrected_codeword to differ from codeword even on some valid error-free codewords, violating FR2's requirement that corrected_codeword equal codeword unchanged when error-free. Detected by the evaluator's exhaustive 128-vector comparison of corrected_codeword and error_detected against the reference.

Simulation of the 112 single-bit-error codewords will show corrected_codeword[3] never gets flipped when syndrome==3'd4, since the XOR-with-syndrome-match term was removed and replaced with a direct passthrough of codeword[3]. This causes mismatches against the reference on all error cases where the erroneous bit is at 1-indexed position 4 (codeword[3]), violating FR3's requirement that the single erroneous bit be flipped back to recover the valid codeword.

evaluate.py instantiates the submission module by its pinned name 'recovered_decoder' in the generated testbench; renaming the module to 'recovered_decoder_impl' causes iverilog compilation of the testbench to fail (unresolved module reference), which must be graded as a FAIL with a compile-error diagnostic per FR4's requirement that the file contain exactly one module named recovered_decoder with the exact pinned port list.
